questions.stem: In a soil profile, the layer that consists of partially weathered bedrock is the
explanation_steps: The textbook defines the horizons: O = organic litter, A = topsoil, E = zone of eluviation, B = subsoil (zone of illuviation).
'C Horizon: A layer that consists of partially weathered bedrock. R Horizon: a layer that consists of unweathered bedrock.' Answer: E.
tips: Order from the top: O – A – E – B – C – R. C = partly weathered rock, R = solid rock.

similar_questions.stem: The soil layer in which materials washed down from above are deposited (illuviation) is the
explanation_steps: Materials leached from the A/E horizons accumulate in the B horizon (illuviation).
Answer: D.

questions.stem: The majority of world population lives in the continent of
explanation_steps: The textbook: of the population of Asia about 2.5 billion (62%) live in China and India alone; Asia holds about 60% of the world's people.
No other continent comes close. Answer: B.
tips: Asia ≈ 60 % of world population; China and India are the two most populous countries.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following continents is the least populated (excluding Antarctica)?
explanation_steps: Oceania/Australia has well under 1 % of the world's population.
Answer: D.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3.2 The Spatial Pattern of World Population Distribution

questions.stem: The branch of geography that studies the origin and development of landforms is
explanation_steps: The textbook (physical geography sub-divisions): 'Geomorphology: The study of the origin and development of landforms.' Answer: B.
tips: geo = earth, morph = form, logy = study → study of landforms.

similar_questions.stem: The branch of geography that studies the distribution of climates over the earth's surface is
explanation_steps: Climatology is the study of the distribution of climate.
Answer: A.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – The Subject Matter of Geography

questions.stem: The maximum insolation along the Tropic of Capricorn occurs on
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Maximum insolation in the southern hemisphere occurs on December 21 along the Tropic of Capricorn.' On that day the overhead (vertical) sun is at 23½°S.
Answer: B.
tips: June 21 → overhead sun at the Tropic of Cancer; December 21 → Tropic of Capricorn; March 21 and September 23 → equator (equinoxes).

similar_questions.stem: On which date is the noon sun overhead at the equator?
explanation_steps: At the equinoxes (March 21 and September 23) the sun is overhead at the equator.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 2.3 Revolution of the Earth – seasons and insolation

questions.stem: Isohyet is an imaginary line drawn on a map that shows the distribution of
explanation_steps: An isohyet joins places that receive equal amounts of rainfall (the textbook lists isohyets among the key words of the precipitation lesson).
Isotherms show temperature, isobars pressure, isohels sunshine. Answer: C.
tips: hyetos (Greek) = rain. Isotherm – temperature; isobar – pressure; isohyet – rainfall.

similar_questions.stem: Lines on a map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure are called
explanation_steps: Isobars join places of equal pressure.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: A fine-textured soil which becomes sticky during a wet season is called
explanation_steps: Soil texture depends on particle size: sand 0.05–2 mm, silt 0.02–0.05 mm, clay < 0.02 mm (too small to see).
Clay is the finest soil; it holds much water, so it becomes sticky when wet and cracks when dry. Answer: E.
tips: Coarse = sand (drains fast); fine = clay (sticky, holds water); loam = a mixture.

similar_questions.stem: A soil made up of a balanced mixture of sand, silt and clay is called
explanation_steps: Loam is a mixture of sand, silt and clay – the best soil for farming.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Most of the world’s active volcanoes are located along the
explanation_steps: Most active volcanoes (about two-thirds or more) lie in the circum-Pacific belt, the 'Pacific Ring of Fire', where oceanic plates subduct under the surrounding plates.
The other belts have volcanoes too, but not 'most' of them, so 'All of the above' is not the best answer. Answer: C.
tips: Pacific Ring of Fire = most volcanoes AND most earthquakes.

similar_questions.stem: Mount Fuji in Japan and the Andes volcanoes of South America both belong to the
explanation_steps: Japan and the Andes lie around the Pacific Ocean on convergent plate boundaries.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: The G11 text describes volcanism and earthquake belts; the phrase 'Pacific Ring' is general knowledge.

questions.stem: Mount Kilimanjaro is a good example of a
explanation_steps: Volcanic mountains are 'formed when molten materials come out to the surface of the earth and solidify'.
Kilimanjaro (Tanzania, Africa's highest peak) is a volcanic cone built by eruptions in the East African Rift region. Answer: A.
tips: Volcanic: Kilimanjaro, Fuji. Fold: Alps, Himalayas, Atlas. Block: Emba Gedem (Eritrea), Vosges. Residual: eroded remnants.

similar_questions.stem: Emba Gedem near Massawa is given in the textbook as an example of a
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Gedem is an example of Block Mountain in Eritrea.'
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, sedimentary rocks are found in the
explanation_steps: Mesozoic sea: 'Hard outcrops of sandstone are commonly found in the plateaus encircling the upper portion of the Comayli and Hadas valleys such as the Cohaito, Emba Soira, Halay and Dege-a plateaus'.
Sandstone is a sedimentary rock, so both A (Kohaito/Qohaito) and C (Emba Soira) are correct; the Central Plateau and Northern Highlands are mainly Precambrian and basalt. Answer: E.
tips: Sandstone plateaus of the Eastern Highlands: Qohaito, Emba Soira, Halay, Dege-a, around Adi Keih and Senafe.

similar_questions.stem: The oldest sandstone in Eritrea, red or brown in colour, is the
explanation_steps: The first sedimentary rocks laid by the Mesozoic sea were the ferruginous sandstones, the oldest sandstone in Eritrea.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: A type of weathering that <u>does not</u> involve water is known as
explanation_steps: Carbonation, hydration and solution are chemical weathering processes that need water; frost action needs water freezing in cracks.
Exfoliation is mechanical weathering caused by repeated heating and cooling: the outer layers of rock expand and peel off – common in hot deserts. It needs no water. Answer: D.
tips: Exfoliation = 'onion weathering' by temperature change (deserts).

similar_questions.stem: Water freezing in the cracks of rocks, expanding and breaking them is called
explanation_steps: When water in cracks freezes it expands by about 10 % and splits the rock.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> an external force?
explanation_steps: The textbook: internal forces originate from the interior of the earth (folding, faulting, volcanism, earthquakes); external forces lower the heights of mountains and fill low areas (weathering, erosion, deposition).
Volcanism is an internal (tectonic) force. Answer: A.
tips: Internal = builds up relief (from inside the earth). External = wears down relief (gradation).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is an internal (tectonic) force?
explanation_steps: Faulting is caused by forces inside the earth.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: Deposition of sediments by a stream takes place mainly in the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Most sediments are deposited on the sea bed or in the lower course of a river after being transported by rivers.'
In the lower course the gradient and speed are low, so the load is dropped (flood plains, levees, deltas). Answer: A.
tips: Upper course – vertical erosion; middle – lateral erosion; lower – deposition.

similar_questions.stem: Which feature is formed in the lower course of a river?
explanation_steps: Deltas form where the river deposits its load at the mouth.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: A main type of erosion by sea is
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the processes of wave erosion: hydraulic action (waves compress air in cracks), corrosion/abrasion (waves hurl rock fragments), attrition (fragments grind each other smaller) and solvent (solution) action.
All four are types of marine erosion. Answer: E. (The paper prints 'coirosion' – read corrosion.)
tips: Wave erosion: hydraulic action, abrasion/corrosion, attrition, solution.

similar_questions.stem: The process in which rock fragments carried by waves collide and become smaller and rounder is
explanation_steps: Attrition wears the load itself down into rounded pebbles and sand.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Gradation by the Action of Waves

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> a wave-depositional feature?
explanation_steps: A sea cliff is formed by wave erosion (undercutting and collapse of the coast).
Beaches, spits and bars are built by wave deposition. Answer: A.
tips: Erosional: cliff, wave-cut platform, cave, arch, stack. Depositional: beach, spit, bar, tombolo.

similar_questions.stem: A low narrow ridge of sand joined to the land at one end and projecting into the sea is a
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'A spit is a low and narrow ridge of pebbles or sand particles joined to the land at one end.'
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Gradation by the Action of Waves

questions.stem: A population pyramid that shows slow population growth and smaller number of young people is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Constrictive: It indicates slow population growth and smaller number of people of younger age.'
Expansive = broad base, fast growth; stationary = nearly equal numbers in all age groups. Answer: B.
tips: Expansive (triangle) → developing countries. Constrictive (narrow base) → slow growth. Stationary → zero growth.

similar_questions.stem: Developing countries are best represented by which type of population pyramid?
explanation_steps: High birth rates give a broad base – the expansive type.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 3.4 Population Growth and Structure – population pyramids

questions.stem: The largest portion of the atmosphere is occupied by a layer known as the
explanation_steps: The textbook: the troposphere extends upwards from the earth's surface 'and it contains more than 75% of the atmosphere'.
(By thickness the thermosphere is deeper, but the textbook's measure is the share of the atmosphere – its mass/gases – which is in the troposphere.) Answer: A.
tips: Troposphere: lowest layer, > 75 % of the air, all weather; temperature falls 6.5 °C per 1000 m.

similar_questions.stem: The layer of the atmosphere in which almost all weather phenomena occur is the
explanation_steps: Clouds, rain and storms form in the troposphere, which holds nearly all the water vapour.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Consider the following population data for a certain country for a specific year: Birth Rate = 25 per 1,000; Death Rate = 12 per 1,000. What is the rate of the natural increase of population of the country during the specific year?
explanation_steps: Natural increase = birth rate − death rate = 25 − 12 = 13 per 1,000.
As a percentage: 13 ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 1.3 %. Answer: B.
tips: Per 1,000 → divide by 10 to get per cent (per 100).

similar_questions.stem: A country has a crude birth rate of 42 per 1,000 and a crude death rate of 14 per 1,000. Its rate of natural increase is

questions.stem: Winds that originate from the sub-tropical high pressure and blow toward the doldrums are called the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Both the Northeast trade winds and Southeast trade winds meet in the doldrums' – they blow from the sub-tropical highs (horse latitudes) to the equatorial low.
The westerlies blow from the sub-tropical highs towards the sub-polar lows. Answer: A.
tips: Sub-tropical high → equator = trade winds; → sub-polar low = westerlies; polar high → sub-polar low = polar easterlies.

similar_questions.stem: Winds that blow from the sub-tropical high pressure belts towards the sub-polar low pressure belts are the
explanation_steps: The westerlies originate from the horse latitudes and blow poleward.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The type of soil erosion created when raindrops strike the ground is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Splash Erosion: The direct collision of raindrops with the ground, causing soil particles to' be thrown up and moved. Answer: B.
tips: Five types in the textbook: sheet, splash, rill, gully, wind.

similar_questions.stem: The removal of topsoil by rain water uniformly from the surface is
explanation_steps: Sheet erosion removes a thin even layer of topsoil.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The submerged portion of a continent is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Continental shelf is a submerged part of the continent. It is an extension of the continent that is covered with shallow water.' Answer: C.
tips: Shelf (shallow, gentle) → slope (steep) → abyssal plain (deep ocean floor).

similar_questions.stem: The steep part of the ocean floor between the continental shelf and the deep ocean floor is the
explanation_steps: Beyond the shelf edge the sea floor drops steeply – the continental slope.
Answer: A.

questions.stem: A wind that blows from the floor of a valley to the mountain slope is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: the wind that blows during the day 'from the valley floor to the mountain slopes is called a valley breeze or anabatic wind'.
At night cold air drains downslope – the mountain breeze or katabatic wind. Answer: D.
tips: ana = up (anabatic, day); kata = down (katabatic, night).

similar_questions.stem: Cold air flowing down a mountain slope into the valley at night is called
explanation_steps: At night the slopes cool quickly and dense air drains downhill – katabatic (mountain) wind.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 3.4 Local winds – mountain and valley breezes

questions.stem: The two most populated countries in Asia are
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Of the population of Asia, for example, about 2.5 billion or 62% live in China and India alone.' Answer: C.
tips: China and India are the two most populous countries in the world as well as in Asia.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these countries has the largest population in Africa?
explanation_steps: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country (listed among the ten most populated countries in the textbook table).
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following climatic divisions is considered the most severe?
explanation_steps: In the polar climates (tundra and ice cap) the textbook says of the ice cap: 'the land is permanently covered with ice and snow. It is the most severe of the earth’s climates and is found in Greenland and in most of Antarctica.' Answer: E.
tips: Ice cap (a polar climate) = the most severe climate on earth.

similar_questions.stem: The ice cap climate is found mainly in
explanation_steps: The textbook: found in Greenland and most of Antarctica.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates

questions.stem: The most common types of village settlements in coastal Eritrea are
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Fishing villages develop in places where fishing is the major occupation. Such villages are sited on river' banks, lake shores and sea coasts.
Along the Eritrean Red Sea coast and islands the villages are mainly fishing villages. Answer: A.
tips: Match the village type to the main occupation of the area.

similar_questions.stem: Villages that grow up around a quarry or mine are called
explanation_steps: The function of the settlement names the village type.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 4.2 Rural Settlements – functional types of villages

questions.stem: A type of plateau formed when old plateaus are completely eroded and reduced in height is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Residual plateaus are plateaus formed when old plateaus are tremendously eroded and reduced in height.' Answer: E.
tips: Intermontane = surrounded by mountains; piedmont = at the foot of mountains; volcanic = lava; residual = worn-down remnant.

similar_questions.stem: A plateau enclosed by mountains on all sides, such as the Tibetan Plateau, is a(n)
explanation_steps: Intermontane = between mountains.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The most widely used measure of economic development is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Per capita income is a widely used economic measure of development. It is the total yearly income of a country … divided by the total population.' Answer: A.
tips: Economic measures: per capita income, employment structure, energy consumption. Social measures: literacy, life expectancy, calories, HDI.

similar_questions.stem: Per capita income is calculated by

options.B: dividing the total yearly income of a country by its population

explanation_steps: Per capita = per head: total income ÷ population.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Thar Desert is found in
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the dry climates' deserts: Sahara, Kalahari and Namib (Africa), the Arabian desert, the 'Thar desert in northeast India', Mohave/Colorado (North America)…
India is in Asia. Answer: B. (The Thar lies on the India–Pakistan border in north-west India.)
tips: Africa: Sahara, Kalahari, Namib. Asia: Arabian, Thar, Gobi. Australia: Great Australian deserts. S. America: Atacama, Patagonia.

similar_questions.stem: The Atacama Desert is found in
explanation_steps: The Atacama lies on the west coast of South America (Chile).
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates
textbook_ref.note: The textbook places the Thar in 'northeast India'; it actually lies in north-west India/Pakistan. Either way the continent is Asia.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> a form of precipitation?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Precipitation includes rain, snow, hail, sleet, fogs, mist, dew etc.'
Hail, rainfall, sleet and snow are all forms of precipitation, so none of A–D is the answer. Answer: E.
tips: When every listed item belongs to the group, choose 'None of the above'.

similar_questions.stem: Frozen raindrops, or a mixture of rain and snow, falling to the ground is called
explanation_steps: Sleet = rain and snow together / frozen raindrops.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The process in which heat is transferred from one object into another through direct contact is known as
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Transfer of heat from one object to another by contact is called conduction.' The air in contact with the ground is heated by conduction. Answer: B.
tips: Conduction = contact; convection = rising currents; radiation = waves through space.

similar_questions.stem: Heat transfer by the vertical movement of heated air is called
explanation_steps: Warm air rises and cold air sinks – convection currents.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Winds that blow from the fast rotating part of the Earth (the equator) to the slow rotating part (pole), deflect towards
explanation_steps: The earth rotates from west to east, and the equator moves eastward faster than higher latitudes.

Air moving from the equator towards the poles keeps its greater eastward speed, so it runs ahead of the surface – it is deflected towards the east (to the right in the N. Hemisphere, to the left in the S. Hemisphere; e.g. the westerlies).
Winds blowing towards the equator lag behind and are deflected west (e.g. NE and SE trade winds). Answer: C.
tips: Coriolis effect: poleward winds turn east, equatorward winds turn west.

similar_questions.stem: The north-east trade winds get their direction because air moving towards the equator is deflected to the
explanation_steps: Equatorward air comes from slower-moving latitudes and lags behind the faster surface → deflected west; blowing from the NE.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 2.2 Effects of Rotation – deflection of wind

questions.review_flag: The textbook explains the Coriolis effect only as 'right in the northern / left in the southern hemisphere'; the 'deflect towards east' conclusion (Ferrel's law for poleward winds) is reasoned, not quoted.

questions.stem: One of the following <u>is not</u> a factor in the formation of a soil.
explanation_steps: The textbook gives five interactive soil-forming factors: parent material, climate, relief (topography), living organisms and time.
Climate, relief, living things and parent material are all factors, so none of A–D is the answer. Answer: E.
tips: Five soil-forming factors: parent material, climate, relief, organisms, time.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is one of the five soil-forming factors?
explanation_steps: Soils need thousands of years to develop – time is a factor.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: According to the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the minimum daily requirement of calories for a person is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'According to the Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO), 2360 calories a day per person is the minimum requirement for healthy life.' Answer: B.
tips: USA ≈ 3700 calories a day; sub-Saharan Africa ≤ 2000; FAO minimum 2360.

similar_questions.stem: If daily calorie availability in a country is 3700, by how much does it exceed the FAO minimum?
explanation_steps: 3700 − 2360 = 1340 calories (about 57 % above the minimum).
Answer: A.

questions.stem: In sea breeze, winds blow from
explanation_steps: The textbook: by day the land heats faster than the sea, which 'causes winds to blow from sea to land, which is known as sea breezes'. Answer: C.
tips: Sea breeze – day – sea to land. Land breeze – night – land to sea.

similar_questions.stem: A land breeze blows

options.A: from sea to land during the day
options.B: from land to sea at night
options.C: from land to sea during the day
options.D: from sea to land at night

explanation_steps: At night the land cools faster, so pressure is higher over land and air flows to the sea.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 2.2 Effects of Rotation – land and sea breezes

questions.stem: Rocky Mountains are found in the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Rocky Mountains: These are found in the western coast of North America. Rocky Mountains stretch for about 5,300 kilometers from north to south.' Answer: A.
tips: Rockies – W. North America; Andes – W. South America; Alps – S. Europe; Himalayas – S. Asia.

similar_questions.stem: The Andes Mountains are found along the
explanation_steps: The Andes run north–south along the west of South America.
Answer: A.

questions.stem: In which of the following places are earthquakes less frequent?
explanation_steps: Earthquakes happen mainly along plate boundaries (margins), including the Himalayan and Andes belts where plates collide.
The stable interiors of continental plates, far from boundaries, have few earthquakes. Answer: B.
tips: Earthquake belts = plate boundaries: circum-Pacific (Andes, Japan), Alpine–Himalayan, mid-ocean ridges.

similar_questions.stem: Most earthquakes on earth occur
explanation_steps: Stress builds and is released where plates meet.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 1.5.2 Distribution of earthquakes in the world

questions.stem: The distribution of population is affected by
explanation_steps: The textbook's factors affecting population distribution and density: climate, relief, vegetation, soils, energy resources and minerals, water supply (plus social and economic factors).
Topography (relief), climate, water and fertile land are all factors. Answer: E.
tips: Physical factors: climate, relief, vegetation, soils, minerals, water.

similar_questions.stem: Why are the frozen tundra regions sparsely populated?

options.B: Harsh cold climate and poor soils

explanation_steps: Extreme cold, frozen ground and short growing seasons discourage settlement.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3.1 Factors Affecting Population Distribution and Density

questions.stem: The East African Rift system is found along the
explanation_steps: At divergent boundaries plates move apart; on land this produces rift valleys such as the East African Rift and the Red Sea trough.
Answer: C. (The paper prints the fifth option as a second 'C. B and C'; shown here as E.)
tips: Divergent → rift valleys and mid-ocean ridges; convergent → fold mountains, trenches; transform → faults like San Andreas.

similar_questions.stem: The Red Sea trough was formed by
explanation_steps: The African and Arabian plates are moving apart.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The basic factor that influences the selection of rural settlements is
explanation_steps: The textbook section '4.2.1 Basic factors that determine the site of rural settlements' lists water supply, availability of cultivable land and pasture, building materials, topography/relief (dry sites, defence, etc.).
All the options are basic site factors, so the best answer is E. Water supply is listed first ('Human beings cannot survive without water'), so A is also accepted.
tips: When the textbook lists several 'basic factors', 'All of the above' is usually intended.

similar_questions.stem: Settlements located close to rivers, lakes and springs are called
explanation_steps: The textbook: settlements found close to sources of water are called water-based or wet-point settlements.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 4.2.1 Basic factors that determine the site of rural settlements

questions.review_flag: Singular stem ('The basic factor') but the textbook lists several basic factors; keyed E (All of the above), A (water supply, listed first) accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: The Rift Valley was mainly formed during the ______ Period.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Another important feature formed during the Miocene Epoch of Tertiary Period was the rift valley.' Answer: B.
tips: Cenozoic = Tertiary + Quaternary. Tertiary events in Eritrea: maximum uplift, Oligocene basalts, Miocene rift valley.

similar_questions.stem: The oldest basalt and trachyte covers of Eritrea were formed during the
explanation_steps: Molten basalt and trachyte poured out through fractures in the Oligocene.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The type of settlement with the shortest duration of stay is referred to as
explanation_steps: The textbook classifies rural settlements by duration: 'Ephemeral, if they last 1–7 days in a particular place; Temporary, if they last 1–30 days' … then seasonal, semi-permanent and permanent.
Ephemeral is the shortest. Answer: B.
tips: Duration order: ephemeral < temporary < seasonal < semi-permanent < permanent.

similar_questions.stem: A rural settlement occupied for only part of the year (e.g. during the rainy season) is called
explanation_steps: Seasonal settlements are used during one season each year.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The form of settlement created when houses are built along a river side, is known as
explanation_steps: The textbook: '1. Linear form: Here villages or hamlets develop in one direction due to the presence of' an attraction such as a river, road, railway or coast.
Houses strung out along a river bank form a linear pattern. Answer: D.
tips: Linear – along a river/road/coast; star-shaped – along several roads meeting at a centre; nucleated – clustered.

similar_questions.stem: A village whose houses spread out along several roads leading from a central market place has a
explanation_steps: Roads radiating from a centre give the star shape.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The natural environment is continuously being modified by
explanation_steps: Unit 5 (Cultural impact on the physical environment) describes how overgrazing, woodcutting/deforestation, desertification and global climate change all alter the natural environment.
Every option modifies the environment. Answer: E.
tips: Human-caused environmental change: deforestation, overgrazing, desertification, pollution, global warming.

similar_questions.stem: The expansion of desert conditions into semi-arid land, accelerated by overgrazing and woodcutting, is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: the spread of the Sahara 'has been accelerated by overgrazing and woodcutting'.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 5 – Cultural Impact on Physical Environment

questions.stem: Which of the following economic activities is more dependent on nature?
explanation_steps: Nomadic pastoralists move with their herds in search of natural pasture and water – they depend directly on rainfall and natural grass.
Dairy farming uses planted fodder and stalls, irrigation supplies water artificially, and manufacturing depends least on nature. Answer: A.
tips: The less technology is used, the more an activity depends on nature (gathering, hunting, nomadism).

similar_questions.stem: Which activity uses technology to reduce dependence on rainfall?
explanation_steps: Irrigation brings water to crops independently of rain.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 5 – Cultural Impact on Physical Environment
textbook_ref.note: Reasoned from the textbook's discussion of technology and environment; the comparison itself is not stated in the text.

questions.stem: Of the following, the country that is the farthest from Eritrea is
explanation_steps: Sudan borders Eritrea; Egypt, Somalia and Kenya are in north-east/east Africa, within about 1,000–2,000 km.
South Africa lies at the southern tip of the continent, more than 5,000 km away. Answer: D.
tips: Use the latitude: Eritrea ≈ 12–18°N; South Africa ≈ 22–35°S.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following countries shares a border with Eritrea?

G lies at the narrow neck where the contours of hill E (south) and the closed loops around P (north) pinch together; land rises to both of them and falls to the west and east. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Describe in brief the following branches of modern geography: 1.1 Economic Geography; 1.2 Urban Geography. (2 points)
questions.answer: 1.1 Economic Geography is the study of the distribution of economic activities such as agriculture, manufacturing and mining (production, exchange and consumption of goods). 1.2 Urban Geography is the study of the origin, site, shape (growth) and classification of towns and cities.
explanation_steps: The textbook (human geography sub-divisions): 'Economic Geography: is the study of the distribution of economic activities such as agriculture, manufacturing and mining.'
'Urban Geography: the study of the origin, site, shape and classification of towns and cities.'
marking_points: 1 point: Economic geography – distribution of economic activities (agriculture, manufacturing, mining…)
1 point: Urban geography – origin, site, shape/growth and classification of towns and cities
tips: Both are branches of human geography; give the textbook definition with one example each.

similar_questions.stem: Describe briefly: (a) Population Geography, (b) Political Geography.
similar_questions.answer: (a) The study of the number, distribution, density, growth, composition and migration of people. (b) The study of states, boundaries, and the political organisation of space.
explanation_steps: Both belong to human geography (G9 Unit 1).

questions.stem: What are the important factors that affect the climate of a place? (2 points)
questions.answer: Latitude; altitude (height above sea level); distance from the sea (continentality); ocean currents; prevailing winds; relief/aspect (mountain barriers); insolation. Any four (½ point each).
explanation_steps: The textbook: temperature/climate differs from place to place; 'the factors for this change are (a) latitude, (b) altitude, (c) ocean currents, (d) distance from the sea, (e) insolation or incoming solar radiation, (f) prevailing winds' and relief.
e.g. higher latitude → less insolation; higher altitude → cooler (6.5 °C per 1000 m); places near the sea have a moderate climate; warm/cold currents warm/cool coasts.
marking_points: ½ point each for any four: latitude; altitude; distance from the sea; ocean currents; prevailing winds; relief/mountain barriers; insolation
tips: 2 points usually = four factors × ½ point. Name the factor and, if space allows, its effect.

similar_questions.stem: Explain how altitude affects the temperature of a place.
similar_questions.answer: Temperature decreases with height at about 6.5 °C per 1000 m (lapse rate), because the air higher up is thinner and holds less heat/water vapour and is farther from the ground that heats it.
explanation_steps: G9 Unit 3 – altitude and temperature.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3 Factors that influence the temperature of a place

questions.stem: Describe <u>any two</u> characteristics of a developing country. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two, e.g.: low per capita income; rapid population growth with a young (expansive) population; most people work in agriculture (low share of industry and services); low literacy and poor health services/low life expectancy; low calorie intake (below 2360); low energy consumption; unemployment and under-use of resources; dependence on exporting raw materials.
explanation_steps: The textbook's measures of development: per capita income, employment structure (e.g. more than 75% in agriculture in Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Eritrea, Chad), energy consumption, nutrition, literacy and health.
Developing countries 'are represented best by expansive types of population pyramids' and suffer rapid population growth and unemployment.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two valid characteristics with a short description (low income; rapid population growth; agricultural employment; low literacy/health; low calories/energy use; unemployment)
tips: Describe = one sentence per characteristic, not just a word.

similar_questions.stem: Give two characteristics of a developed country.
similar_questions.answer: High per capita income; most people work in industry and services; high literacy and life expectancy; slow population growth (constrictive/stationary pyramid); high energy consumption.
explanation_steps: The opposite of the developing-country indicators.

questions.stem: Give <u>three</u> examples of natural hazards that result in loss of life and destruction of property. (1.5 points)
questions.answer: Any three: earthquakes; volcanic eruptions; floods; droughts; tropical storms (cyclones/hurricanes); tsunamis; landslides.
explanation_steps: The G11 textbook describes earthquakes ('The damage earthquakes cause', e.g. Bam, Iran: 80% of the city destroyed) and volcanic eruptions; floods and droughts are hazards discussed with climate and rivers.
marking_points: ½ point each for any three: earthquake; volcanic eruption; flood; drought; storm/cyclone/hurricane; tsunami; landslide
tips: ½ point per correct hazard.

similar_questions.stem: Name two effects of an earthquake on people.
similar_questions.answer: Loss of life and injury; destruction of buildings, roads and bridges; fires; homelessness; disease after the disaster.
explanation_steps: G11 1.5.1 The damage earthquakes cause.

questions.stem: List the main factors that affect population distribution on the Earth’s surface. (2 points)
questions.answer: Physical factors: climate; relief (landforms); vegetation; soils; energy resources and minerals; water supply. Human factors: economic activities/industry, transport, history, government policy. Any four (½ point each).
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'All factors affecting population distribution and density can be classified into the following: i. Climate, ii. Relief, iii. Vegetation, iv. Soils, v. Energy Resources and Minerals, vi. Water Supply' (plus social/economic factors).
marking_points: ½ point each for any four: climate; relief; vegetation; soils; minerals/energy; water supply; (economic/social factors)
tips: Use the textbook list; 2 points = four factors.

similar_questions.stem: Why are river valleys and plains usually densely populated?
similar_questions.answer: Flat land, fertile alluvial soils, water supply for drinking and irrigation, and easy transport.
explanation_steps: G10 3.3.1 Factors affecting population distribution.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3.1 Factors Affecting Population Distribution and Density

questions.stem: List the <u>two</u> major characteristics of the world’s great mountain systems. (2 points)
questions.answer: (1) They are made of sedimentary rocks (e.g. the Alps, Himalayas, Rockies, Andes), which shows that they were formed under the sea. (2) They are arc-shaped (curved) and run in a north–south or east–west direction (Alps, Himalayas, Atlas east–west; Rockies, Andes, Great Dividing Range north–south).
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'All the great mountain systems of the world have the following characteristics: i. The great mountain systems are made of sedimentary rocks … which indicates that they were formed under the sea. ii. All these important mountain systems are arc-shaped (curved) and run in north-south or east-west direction.'
marking_points: 1 point: made of sedimentary rocks / formed under the sea
1 point: arc-shaped (curved) and run N–S or E–W
tips: The question asks for 'the two' – exactly the textbook's two points.

similar_questions.stem: Name two great mountain systems that run north–south.
similar_questions.answer: The Rockies and the Andes (also the Great Dividing Range).
explanation_steps: G9 5.2 Mountains.

textbook_ref.section: 5.2 Mountains – characteristics of the great mountain systems

questions.stem: Name <u>three</u> factors that make flood plains of rivers suitable for agriculture. (1.5 points)
questions.answer: Any three: fertile alluvial soil renewed by floods; flat (level) land that is easy to plough and irrigate; availability of water from the river for irrigation; deep, fine-textured soils that hold moisture.
explanation_steps: The textbook: a flood plain is 'built up by alluvium deposited on the valley floor after flooding. Flood plains have fertile soil.'
Flat terrain and nearby river water make cultivation and irrigation easy (G11 settlement factors: 'Arable land is the result of a combination of fertile soil, nearly flat terrain and good rainfall').
marking_points: ½ point each: fertile alluvial soil; flat land; water for irrigation (or deep moisture-holding soil)
tips: ½ point per factor.

similar_questions.stem: How is a flood plain formed?
similar_questions.answer: In the lower course, when the river floods it spreads over the valley floor and deposits alluvium; repeated floods build a wide flat plain.
explanation_steps: G11 2.2 Features in the lower course.

questions.stem: Give <u>two</u> reasons that make the Southern Plateau of Eritrea have a high potential for crop growing. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two: flat topography (almost a true plateau, little dissection); adequate rainfall; fertile black (basaltic) soils.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The Southern Plateau is agriculturally rich because of its flat topography, adequate rainfall and fertile black soils.'
marking_points: 1 point each for any two: flat topography; adequate rainfall; fertile black (basaltic) soils
tips: Quote the textbook's three reasons; any two earn full marks.

similar_questions.stem: Why is the Mereb Trough potentially rich for agriculture?
similar_questions.answer: Its topography, thick alluvial soils and the presence of the Mereb river.
explanation_steps: G11 7.1 (f) The Mereb Trough.

questions.stem: List <u>any two</u> factors that aggravate soil erosion. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two: deforestation (removal of vegetation cover); overgrazing; ploughing steep slopes / ploughing up and down the slope; heavy (torrential) rainfall on bare soil; strong winds in dry areas; poor farming methods (e.g. no terraces, bush burning).
explanation_steps: The textbook (soil erosion): erosion is the removal of soil by water, wind and ice; it is speeded up where vegetation is removed and where 'the furrows follow up and down the slope'. Conservation methods (terracing, contour ploughing, afforestation) work by reversing these factors.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two: deforestation; overgrazing; ploughing steep slopes/up-and-down; heavy rain on bare soil; wind in dry areas; bush burning
tips: Human causes are the usual expected answers: deforestation, overgrazing, poor ploughing.

similar_questions.stem: Give two methods of soil conservation.
similar_questions.answer: Terracing; contour ploughing; afforestation/reforestation; check dams; controlled grazing; strip cropping.
explanation_steps: G10 2.6 Soil erosion and conservation.

questions.stem: Explain why information on population characteristics is important for development. (3 points)
questions.answer: Adequate information on population characteristics (size, growth, age–sex structure, distribution) enables a country to plan properly for its present and future development. Governments need population data to integrate population factors into planning and policy making – e.g. how many schools, teachers, health centres, houses, jobs and how much food are needed, and where. Ministries such as health, housing, tourism, labour and education need it for their projects, since development projects aim to change the quality of life of the people.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Adequate information of population characteristics enables any country to plan properly for its present and future development. Governments require population data to integrate population factors into their planning and policy making processes. Government institutions like health, housing, tourism, labor, education, and more, need specialists in population studies to carry out many of their projects.'
marking_points: 1 point: enables proper planning for present and future development
1 point: governments integrate population data into policies/planning
1 point: example – services (schools, health, housing, jobs, food) planned by ministries
tips: 3 points: planning; policy making; examples of services (education, health, housing, jobs).

similar_questions.stem: Why is it difficult to give precise population statistics for Eritrea?
similar_questions.answer: Because no official population census has been undertaken in Eritrea; figures are estimates.
explanation_steps: G12 Unit 7.
